definitions: A major neural pathway that originates in the cerebral cortex and descends to the spinal cord, primarily involved in voluntary motor control.
A descending motor pathway responsible for carrying motor information from the brain to the spinal cord, enabling fine motor skills and skilled movements.
examples: Damage to the corticospinal tract can result in paralysis.
The corticospinal tract plays a crucial role in voluntary movement.
Neuroscientists study the development of the corticospinal tract.
